title: Economy & Finance
intro: Economy questions test concepts and institutions, not calculation: what GDP means, how the RBI works, what a Budget contains, and how India plans its growth. Learn the vocabulary precisely — the difference between fiscal and monetary policy, between direct and indirect tax — and attach each institution to its role and head. The facts are stable year to year, so a focused revision here pays off reliably.

items.name: GDP
items.formula: value of all final goods & services produced within a country in a year

items.name: Monetary policy
items.formula: controlled by the RBI (repo rate, CRR, etc.)

items.name: Indirect tax
items.formula: GST (One Nation One Tax, from 1 July 2017)

topics.name: Basic Economic Concepts
topics.details: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year; GNP adds net income from abroad. An economy has three sectors — primary (agriculture), secondary (industry) and tertiary (services); services contribute the largest share of India's GDP.

topics.name: Banking & RBI
topics.details: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), established in 1935 and nationalised in 1949, is the central bank: it issues currency, controls monetary policy, and acts as banker to the government. Its main tools are the repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR and SLR.

solved.solution: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India).

topics.name: Budget, Tax & Fiscal Policy
topics.details: The Union Budget (Article 112) is the government's annual financial statement, presented by the Finance Minister, usually on 1 February. Taxes are direct (income, corporate) or indirect (GST, launched 1 July 2017).

solved.problem: Under which article is the Union Budget presented?

topics.name: National Income & Planning
topics.details: India followed Five-Year Plans (the first began in 1951) under the Planning Commission, which was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015. Per capita income is national income divided by population. The Census of India is conducted every ten years.

shortcuts: Learn the vocabulary precisely — fiscal (govt spending) vs monetary (RBI) policy.
Direct tax = income/corporate; indirect tax = GST (1 July 2017).
RBI tools: repo, reverse repo, CRR, SLR.
Services (tertiary) sector is the largest in India's GDP.
Planning Commission → NITI Aayog (2015); Census every 10 years.
mistakes: Confusing fiscal policy (government) with monetary policy (RBI).
Calling GST a direct tax — it is indirect.
Mixing up GDP (within the country) and GNP (adds income from abroad).
Forgetting NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
pyq: SSC asks definitions (GDP, inflation, sectors), RBI tools, tax types (GST), and institution facts (NITI Aayog, SEBI, NABARD). These are stable, high-return facts.
summary: Economy is concepts and institutions: GDP/inflation/sectors, the RBI and its monetary tools, the Budget with direct vs indirect tax (GST), and planning bodies (NITI Aayog). Learn the definitions exactly and tie each institution to its role — the facts barely change year to year.
